headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: Gemini CLI can ingest shared files/MCP outputs while Prefect can operationalize them, creating unsafe default interaction paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI reads/writes repo files, uses MCP, and shares state via filesystem/git; Prefect can consume workflow metadata and call APIs. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs is treated as instructions. The pair interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or repo checkout
IF Gemini CLI ingests MCP/file content as instructions without provenance checks
IF Prefect reads that content into downstream workflow steps
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access between the agents
Route MCP outputs through a provenance-tagged staging file
Require explicit human review before Prefect consumes Gemini-generated text
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
requires-engineering: add content-signing or allowlist parsing for instruction-like fields

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and has broad network egress; Prefect touches workflow metadata and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive files can flow from Gemini into Prefect outputs or API calls. The profiles do not show PHI or secrets by default, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same directory tree
IF Gemini CLI processes files containing secrets or sensitive source code
IF Prefect exports or logs workflow metadata to external services
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared checkout
Run Prefect and Gemini under separate service accounts
Turn off or restrict external logging for workflows handling sensitive metadata
Use a throwaway workspace for Gemini-generated artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before any API egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses; its concurrency model says shared state is via filesystem and git only. Prefect is an orchestrator that can also act on shared mutable resources. That overlap makes concurrent writes and git-state races dangerous in default setups, with possible irreversible repo corruption or conflicting automation.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or working directory
IF Prefect tasks mutate files or repo state while Gemini CLI is active
IF no external locking or serialization is configured
mitigations: Serialize access with a single writer lock
Assign separate branches or worktrees per agent
Pause Prefect runs while Gemini edits the repo
Use read-only mounts for one agent
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell commands, and file edits; Prefect can orchestrate downstream actions. If Prefect treats Gemini output as authoritative, a bad suggestion can cascade into automated execution or deployment-like workflows. The pair therefore has a default dangerous path unless explicit verification is inserted.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes Gemini-produced text or files as workflow inputs
IF Prefect executes tasks without a verification gate
IF Gemini output contains an incorrect command, config, or code change
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before execution
Require schema validation on Gemini-produced artifacts
Limit Prefect to dry-run mode for Gemini outputs
Log and diff all generated changes before applying them
requires-engineering: add automated verification against tests or policy checks

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is documented for either agent. Gemini CLI handles source code and shell environment; Prefect handles workflow metadata. Without evidence of PHI, EU PII, or conflicting retention policies, only a low compliance risk is supported, and the other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data-flow dependent.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF Prefect logs or retains that data longer than Gemini's local handling
IF the deployment crosses a residency boundary not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Review logging and retention settings before use
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated workloads
Document data-flow boundaries for operators
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
